draft.title: What popular culture is
card: Popular culture is the music, film, games, sport, fashion and media that large numbers of people enjoy. It is part of everyday life for many people.
It is often spread through mass media, which are channels that reach large audiences, such as television, radio, streaming services and social media.
What makes something popular culture is how widely it is shared and enjoyed, not how old, costly or serious it is.
Popular culture changes over time. Songs, games and fashions can rise quickly and then fade as audiences move on.
draft.remember: Popular culture is what large numbers of people enjoy, often shared through mass media.

a.q: Which of these is the best example of popular culture?
opts: A chart-topping song streamed by millions of listeners
A private family recipe passed down for generations
A rare painting held in a locked collection
A school rule about wearing the uniform
a.why: A song streamed by millions is enjoyed by large numbers of people and spread through mass media. The family recipe is a cultural practice, but it is not shared by large numbers of people through mass media.
a.clue: Look for what is enjoyed by a large audience.

b.q: Dana says a film cannot be popular culture because it is old. Which reply is the most accurate?
opts: Age does not decide it, wide enjoyment by many people does
Age does decide it, because only new films are shared
Only films shown on television count as popular culture
It is popular culture only if critics rate it highly
b.why: Popular culture is defined by how widely it is enjoyed, so an old film that many people still watch can count. Critics' ratings are tempting but do not decide it, because the idea depends on large audiences, not approval.
b.clue: Think about what the card says makes something popular culture.

a.best: A chart-topping song streamed by millions of listeners

b.best: Age does not decide it, wide enjoyment by many people does

a.q: Kai's band plays its own songs to a few friends in a garage in Wollongong. Which change would make its music popular culture?
opts: Large numbers of people across Australia streaming its songs
Its songs being rewritten to sound more serious in tone
Its concert tickets being sold at a much higher price
Its songs being rewritten about events from decades ago
a.why: Popular culture is defined by how widely something is shared and enjoyed, so the band's music counts once large numbers of people stream it. Making the songs more serious, older in topic or more costly to see changes the music or its price, but not how many people enjoy it.
a.clue: Which change is about the size of the audience?
